why: Drops the try/catch around the start request, so a `WebGLRenderer` that gets its context and then fails to initialise throws out of a HUD click handler with nobody listening. The player sits on a menu whose buttons silently do nothing -- no error page, no report, no clue. This guard is NEW WORK rather than a copy of `boot()`'s own: while the eager start existed, that same failure threw inside `boot()`'s try. Issue #428 turns a documented edge case ('a REPLACEMENT that throws does not arrive here') into the ordinary path. 7 of 76 in the scoped run, RE-DERIVED at issue #325's 2026-09-11 ruling and named rather than counted: `still reports the underlying error`, `registers its teardown even though the start failed`, `handles a thrown non-Error`, the capability suite's `still catches a session that fails for a reason the probe cannot see`, and the #428 suite's `a failed start reaches the same message page`, `a FATAL cause still replaces the page` and `leaves the shell standing when the cause is transient`. IT WAS 8, and the fall is not lost coverage. Three page-renderer cases moved to the BOOT boundary because a transient match failure no longer produces a page to render, and they were never about this guard -- they used a failing match as a convenient trigger. Two cases that ARE about it arrived in their place. The population is better composed at 7 than it was at 8. The find string grew in issue #325, which gave the catch a `'match'` failure point so the screen it raises says the MATCH could not start rather than that the game could not: the guard being mutated is the same one, and the argument is part of it.
